name: WY at-large
label: Safe R

key_factors: Chuck Gray's large fundraising and outside-spending advantage
Prediction markets price Republican win at ~99%
model.rationale: Wyoming's R+23 lean makes this seat effectively unwinnable for a Democrat, and the resource gap is extreme: Gray has raised $1.6 million with nearly $900,000 in outside support, while Lisa Kinney has raised under $20,000. Markets price a Republican win at 99%, so the forecast sits well beyond the baseline's already-safe Republican margin.
model.watch: A major scandal or third-party surge is essentially the only plausible path to narrowing this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Harriet Hageman (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Wyoming's at-large House seat is among the most Republican-held districts in the country, with a partisan lean of R+23. Harriet Hageman is leaving the seat to run for Senate, but the open seat does little to change the picture. Republican Chuck Gray enters the general election with a decisive financial edge, having raised $1.6 million and drawn nearly $900,000 in outside support.

Democrat Lisa Kinney has raised under $20,000 with almost no cash on hand, and no outside spending backs her. Prediction markets give Republicans roughly a 99% chance of holding the seat. With no polls and no expert ratings available, the forecast rests on the district's overwhelming partisan lean and the lopsided resource gap, both pointing to a safe Republican hold.
